clue.text: Vain individual requiring top German wine, reportedly …

indicators.note: reportedly tells us the phrase built from the clue is heard, not written

parts.note: top means peak, and hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A conceited person insists on the best German wine, so people say, and the sentence runs on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, PEAK HOCK sounds like the bird. The trailing dots join this clue to 9 across, whose two dots pick up the thread.
explanation.definitionFit: The peacock, showing off its tail, is the proverbial emblem of vanity, so a vain person is called one.

clue.text: Will's responsible person as Devon banker, dividing gold

parts.note: a banker is a river, something with banks; the Exe flows through Devon
cut is a dividing, as in the cut of the cards
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone acting for a will is cast as a Devon banker splitting up gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is not a financier: in crosswords it is a river, here the Exe.
explanation.definitionFit: An executor is the person named in a will to carry out its instructions.

clue.text: Conservative is in rush to become whip

indicators.note: in tells us the word is goes inside the word for rush

parts.note: haste is hurry or rush

explanation.surface: A Conservative MP hurries to become a party whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip' in the surface is the parliamentary office; as the definition it is the verb meaning to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To whip someone is to punish them, as is to chastise them.

clue.text: Pasta from tin Lionel cooked around noon

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around another
cooked means altered by preparation, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lionel cooked pasta from a tin at lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns LIONEL into NELLOI, which goes 'around' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannelloni are large pasta tubes, usually stuffed and baked.

clue.text: Tolerate rude fellow

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put up with a rude man.
explanation.definitionFit: Bear is both a verb for enduring and a noun for a gruff, ill-mannered person.

clue.text: Extremely sensitive rugby player, 14

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the end letters of the word are kept

parts.note: a wing is a rugby player on the flank

explanation.surface: A rugby player wearing 14, the wing's number, is extremely sensitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is not a shirt number but a pointer to the answer at 14 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing is one example of needlework, the answer to 14 down.

clue.text: Day of rest that occasionally pop group's taken up

indicators.note: taken up in a down clue means lifted, so the letters are read from bottom to top
occasionally means only now and then, so alternate letters are picked

parts.note: Abba's, from the Swedish pop group Abba

explanation.surface: A day off that a pop group sometimes enjoys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' gives HT from that; 'taken up' reverses HTABBAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day set aside for rest and worship.

clue.text: Old nautical instrument remaining after last of bids

indicators.note: after means this piece comes after the other in the answer
last of means only the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: extant means still existing or remaining

explanation.surface: An antique ship's instrument is still around after the final bid at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextant is a navigation tool for measuring the angle of the sun or stars above the horizon at sea.

clue.text: .. drink always imbibed by British date

indicators.note: imbibed by means swallowed by, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a date can be an age or era, as in the Stone Age
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 across: the vain person also takes a drink which a British date always enjoys.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink other than water, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Put on new coat with narrow back, keeping trendy

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the reversed word holds another piece within it
back tells us the word for narrow is read backwards

parts.note: to taper is to narrow
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: Instructions for a tailored jacket: a new coat with a narrow back that stays fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TAPER into REPAT, which keeps IN to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To repaint something is to apply a fresh coat of paint to it.

clue.text: Mammal, rabbit, hid regularly amongst grass all around

indicators.note: all around tells us the whole assembled string is turned round and read backwards
amongst means placed among, so these picked letters go inside the word for grass

parts.note: turf is grass with its roots and soil

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth of the two words

explanation.surface: A mammal and a rabbit hid in the grass all around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks ABTI from rabbit hid; 'amongst' puts it in TURF to give TABTIURF, which 'all around' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit bat is a large bat that feeds on fruit, so it is a mammal.

clue.text: Pet belonging to us feeds at five, roughly

indicators.note: feeds is read as goes into, so one piece is put inside the other
roughly means not exactly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: Our pet gets its food at five o'clock, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges AT FIVE into FAVITE, and 'feeds' puts OUR into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet in the sense of a teacher's pet is a favourite, the one preferred above others.

clue.text: Exert pressure on sleuth somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of the word arrive by some unexplained route, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to lean on a detective in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: To hustle someone is to push or pressure them into acting quickly.

clue.text: Scottish football club being mostly obdurate

parts.note: living can mean existing or being, as in a living thing

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: stony means hard and unyielding, like obdurate

explanation.surface: A Scottish football club is accused of being largely stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of STONY.
explanation.definitionFit: Livingston FC is a Scottish professional football club from the West Lothian town of that name.

clue.text: Criminal world keen to pinch European tapestry, say

indicators.note: to pinch means to grip, so the rearranged letters hold another letter inside
criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The underworld is eager to steal a European tapestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges WORLD KEEN into NEDLEWORK, which grips E.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapestry is an example of decorative work done with a needle and thread, hence the say.

clue.text: Bowls over with second ball turning, claiming wicket

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the turned pair holds another letter inside
turning means the two letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: O is a ball, from its round shape
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler stuns the batsmen with a spinning second delivery that takes a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes OS of S and O, and 'claiming' puts W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To wow people is to impress them greatly, just as bowling them over does.

clue.text: Fifty university fellows blocking review of book earnings

indicators.note: blocking means obstructing by standing in the middle, so these letters sit inside the other word
review is read as re-view, looking back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Fifty academics get in the way of a book review and its earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review of' turns TOME into EMOT, and LUMEN goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An emolument is a salary, fee or other payment for work, a formal word for earnings.

clue.text: Dispense with goalkeeper's pass to team member?

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to get rid of it
in football a ... is the goalkeeper hurling the ball by hand to a teammate

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper is told to do without the pass to a teammate.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to discard something and a goalkeeper's hand-thrown distribution of the ball.

clue.text: Do well, rather like a constituent in Rye?

parts.note: rye bread is made from rye flour, so flour is one of its ingredients
the suffix -ish means rather like, as in boyish

explanation.surface: Someone thrives, rather like an ingredient in rye bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Rye is also a town in Sussex, so the capital helps hide the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish is to thrive or prosper, to do well.

clue.text: Delinquent pair at first illegally entering school

indicators.note: entering means going in, so these letters go inside the word for school

parts.note: a cult is a school of thought or sect

indicators.note: at first means only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A young offender and accomplice break into a school illegally.
explanation.definitionFit: A delinquent, a wrongdoer, is the culprit of an offence.

clue.text: Palace attendant has no time for tour guide

indicators.note: has no means lacks, so the letter for time is removed from the word

parts.note: a courtier attends at a royal court or palace

explanation.surface: A royal attendant is too busy to show visitors round.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier is someone employed to guide and look after a group of tourists.

clue.text: Check hotel key

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A guest is told to check the hotel key.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to stop or halt its progress.

clue.text: Peacekeepers' secretary-general perhaps not confirmed

parts.note: UN is the United Nations, whose troops are peacekeepers
a secretary-general is an example of an official

explanation.surface: The UN's chief may not yet have been confirmed in post.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unofficial lacks formal authorisation or confirmation.

clue.text: Hat for a journalist to wear

indicators.note: to wear means to have on, so the first piece goes round the second as clothing does

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A hat suitable for a reporter to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown and a brim.

clue.text: Going out with sexy body, bust, repeatedly exposed

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of the outer layer, so each word, one after another, loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A racy picture of someone leaving with a sexy body and bust on display.
explanation.definitionFit: An exodus is a mass departure, a going out, after the Israelites leaving Egypt.

clue.text: Terrible despair across America? Bliss!

indicators.note: across means lying over, so the rearranged letters straddle the letter for America
terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cry that dreadful gloom has spread across America turns oddly into bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges DESPAIR into PRADISE, which goes 'across' A.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a state of perfect happiness, the same as bliss.

clue.text: Hands over, making exchange

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: paws are informal for hands

explanation.surface: Someone hands something over to make an exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to trade one thing for another.

clue.text: Type of irrigation restricted by protocol on Iceland

indicators.note: restricted by means confined within, so the answer lies within the run of letters

explanation.surface: A medical procedure is limited by the rules in force in Iceland.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonic irrigation flushes the colon with water, so colonic names that kind.

clue.text: Diamonds, yellowish-white, 99 maybe

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
cream is a yellowish-white colour

explanation.surface: Diamonds of a pale yellow tint, maybe numbering 99.
explanation.walkthrough: A 99 is a British soft-serve ice cream cone with a chocolate flake stuck in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A 99 is one example of the frozen dessert, hence the maybe.

clue.text: Cut broadcaster admits is inadequate

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the broadcaster's name takes the other word inside

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster
to etch is to cut lines into a surface

explanation.surface: A broadcaster admits that its cut programme was not good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketchy means lacking in detail or substance, hence inadequate.
